goal: A food-reference editor wants to describe the evidence for isomaltose hydrolysis in baker's yeast S288C. Have a research colleague trace the primary article's samples, substrates, and what was actually measured. Let that colleague follow up any unresolved attribution directly in the available records. Which entries in the strain's public archive can legitimately be linked to those observations, and what should the editor leave unknown? Give the source locations for the key distinctions and close when the wording can be justified. This is an archival question about published observations.

The IMA4-encoded protein was represented by the identical IMA3 sequence. Separate IMA4 activity and its relative contribution in the native strain remain unknown.
Native whole-cell S288C hydrolysis, native expression of each locus, and the contribution of each locus in yeast or dough remain unmeasured here.

final_decision.rationale: The colleague traced the preparations through the primary article and followed the attribution into the S288C archive. Experimental procedures §§4.2–4.3 identify the plasmid templates, expression host and glucose-release assay. Table 2 and Fig. 1 report isomaltose hydrolysis by Ima1p, Ima2p, Ima3p and Ima5p, corresponding to P53051, Q08295, P0CW40 and P40884. Table 3 reports fits for individual preparations. The Introduction, cloning list and archive sequence digests identify P0CW41 as encoding the same protein as P0CW40, with IMA3 supplying the assayed construct. The archive fields exact_reaction, parents and assay_coverage distinguish enzyme-class links from direct reaction links, named isomaltose entries from other or unresolved substrates, and individual from jointly indexed accessions. The shared P53051/Q08295 affinity entry counts once. The record examples and aggregate coverage leave their strain, preparation, source publication and independence undetermined without further provenance. Empty links leave activity undetermined. Native whole-cell hydrolysis, locus expression and contributions in yeast or dough lie outside these observations. The source locations and attribution limits settle the requested editorial wording.

exploratory_claims.statement: The accession-linked records identify the experimental source strain and preparation of every isomaltose assay, establish independent measurements for every jointly indexed protein, and establish the contribution of each locus to native S288C hydrolysis.
exploratory_claims.scope: Attribution available from the S288C isomaltose archive snapshot and the paper's assays of purified recombinant protein.
exploratory_claims.criteria: Source-level identification would require an assay record naming the preparation and strain. Separate experimental measurements require separate sample identities. A native contribution requires observations in the native biological material.
exploratory_claims.limitations: The lookup gives examples and aggregate coverage. A joint index entry counts once and leaves its underlying measurement provenance open. Empty exact-reaction links and an empty assay list for P0CW41 leave separate activity unresolved. Native expression and locus contributions in yeast or dough remain unknown.

lead_interpretation.rationale: The S288C archive has class links and accession-indexed parameter entries. Its examples include a single-accession isomaltose catalytic-efficiency entry and one isomaltose affinity entry shared between P53051 and Q08295. Other examples name different substrates or leave substrate unresolved. The primary paper names the assayed constructs and reports their kinetics separately.

modules.focus: Trace the biochemical evidence in the 2014 four-isomaltase paper (PMC3953731) from the candidate list. Identify the actual source material and preparations, which isomaltose assays were performed, and how their readouts differ from other substrates and readouts. Follow any unresolved sample-to-locus attribution yourself into the available S288C public records. You can select and execute the relevant archive method directly. decisions.rationale: The candidate page identifies the original by PMCID. The full text can identify the assayed preparations, substrates and readouts. A lookup restricted to isomaltose and S288C can independently resolve which accessions and assay records have individual, group or class-level support.

handoffs.rationale: The colleague traced the preparations through the primary article and followed the attribution into the S288C archive. Experimental procedures §§4.2–4.3 identify the plasmid templates, expression host and glucose-release assay. Table 2 and Fig. 1 report isomaltose hydrolysis by Ima1p, Ima2p, Ima3p and Ima5p, corresponding to P53051, Q08295, P0CW40 and P40884. Table 3 reports fits for individual preparations. The Introduction, cloning list and archive sequence digests identify P0CW41 as encoding the same protein as P0CW40, with IMA3 supplying the assayed construct. The archive fields exact_reaction, parents and assay_coverage distinguish enzyme-class links from direct reaction links, named isomaltose entries from other or unresolved substrates, and individual from jointly indexed accessions. The shared P53051/Q08295 affinity entry counts once. The record examples and aggregate coverage leave their strain, preparation, source publication and independence undetermined without further provenance. Empty links leave activity undetermined. Native whole-cell hydrolysis, locus expression and contributions in yeast or dough lie outside these observations. The source locations and attribution limits settle the requested editorial wording.
